questions.prompt: Getting started. {{situation}} Write a function, {{function}}, for this situation. Then name its quantities and explain what its slope and y-intercept mean.
hints: The independent quantity is the one you choose; the dependent quantity depends on it.
The amount that changes with each unit of the input is the rate: it multiplies the variable.
The amount you start with is added once: it is the value of the function when the input is zero.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. In a linear function rule, the amount added once, at the start, is the…

reasoning: The input (independent quantity) is the one that changes freely; the output (dependent quantity) depends on it.
The rate of change multiplies the variable: it is the slope.
The starting amount is the value when the input is 0: it is the y-intercept.
solutionReview.commonError: Switching the rate and the starting amount — the starting amount is added once, not once for each unit.

questions.prompt: Words to symbols. Write each statement as an inequality, using the variable it names.
hints: “At least” and “no less than” include the number itself, so they use ≥.
“At most” and “no more than” also include the number, so they use ≤.
“More than” and “exceeds” leave the number out (>); “fewer than” and “less than” leave it out too (<).

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. “At least 18” includes 18 itself. Which symbol includes the number?

reasoning: Decide whether the boundary number itself is allowed: “at least” and “at most” include it; “more than” and “fewer than” do not.
Decide the direction: “at least” and “more than” point to greater values; “at most” and “fewer than” to smaller values.
solutionReview.commonError: Writing > for “at least”: “at least 18” includes 18, so it is ≥.

questions.prompt: Hey, I remember this! Solve {{inequality}}. Then graph its solution.
hints: Undo the addition or subtraction first, on both sides.
Then divide both sides by the coefficient of the variable — it is negative, so think about the symbol.
Graph: a closed dot for ≤ or ≥, an open dot for < or >. Test a value from your shaded side in the original inequality.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number…

reasoning: Undo the constant term: add or subtract it on both sides.
Divide both sides by the negative coefficient and reverse the symbol.
Graph the boundary with an open or closed dot and shade toward the solutions; check a test value.
solutionReview.commonError: Keeping the symbol after dividing by a negative number.

sections.title: Classwork — Modeling, Comparing and Solving Inequalities

questions.prompt: Getting Started — Fundraising Function. Elijah’s troop sells popcorn. Identify the quantities, then write the function f(b) for Elijah’s total sales after he sells b boxes, and use it to complete the table.
questions.scenario: Each camper starts with a credit of $25 toward sales, and each box of popcorn sells for $3.75.
questions.equationPrompt: Write the function f(b) for Elijah’s total sales after selling b boxes.
hints: The total depends on how many boxes are sold, so boxes sold is the input.
Every box adds the same amount to the total, and the starting credit is there before any box is sold.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Which amount is added once for EACH box sold?

steps.title: Rate and starting amount
steps.instruction: A linear model has the form f(x) = (rate) · x + (starting amount). The rate multiplies the variable; the starting amount is added once.

reasoning: The total depends on the number of boxes, so boxes sold is the independent quantity and total sales is the dependent quantity.
Each box adds $3.75 and the credit adds $25 once: f(b) = 3.75b + 25.
solutionReview.commonError: Writing f(b) = 25b + 3.75 — the credit is added once, not once per box.

questions.prompt: Activity 3.1 — Elijah has a sales goal of $1,600. The graph shows f(b) = 3.75b + 25 and the horizontal line y = 1600. Use the graph to answer.

responses.label: The point where the horizontal line meets the graph of f(b)
The number of boxes Elijah must sell to make exactly $1,600
Which equation does that point solve?
On a number line, the number of boxes that makes exactly $1,600 is shown with…

hints: Follow the horizontal line from the goal on the vertical axis until it meets the graph of f(b).
Read the input (boxes) of that point from the horizontal axis.
Check your number of boxes by substituting it into f(b).

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The horizontal line marks every point where total sales are…

steps.title: Linear inequality
steps.instruction: A linear inequality is a non-equal comparison of two linear expressions, using <, >, ≤ or ≥. Its solution set is every value that makes it true.

reasoning: The line y = 1600 meets the graph at (420, 1600).
One exact number of boxes is one closed dot on a number line.
solutionReview.commonError: Reading the coordinates in the wrong order — the input (boxes) comes first.

questions.prompt: Graph the numbers of boxes Elijah could sell and still have total sales of $1,600 or less. He cannot sell a negative number of boxes.
hints: Both ends are included: zero boxes, and the number of boxes that makes exactly $1,600.
Use closed dots at both ends, and shade between them.

reasoning: The smallest possible number of boxes is 0, and 420 boxes makes exactly $1,600.
Both ends are included, so both dots are closed, with shading between them: 0 ≤ b ≤ 420.
solutionReview.commonError: Shading left from 420 with an arrow — that includes negative numbers of boxes.

questions.prompt: Graph the numbers of boxes that give Elijah total sales of more than $1,600.
hints: The boundary is where total sales are exactly the goal, but that value is not included.
Use an open dot and shade toward the larger numbers of boxes.

reasoning: The boundary is 420 boxes, which gives exactly $1,600 — not more — so the dot is open.
More boxes give more sales, so shade to the right: b > 420.
solutionReview.commonError: Using a closed dot at 420: “more than $1,600” leaves out exactly $1,600.

questions.prompt: Use the graph of f(b) = 3.75b + 25 to answer each question. Write an equation or an inequality for each answer.

responses.label: How many boxes would Elijah have to sell to earn at least $925?
How many boxes would Elijah have to sell to earn less than $2,050?
How many boxes would Elijah have to sell to earn exactly $700?
Which of your three answers is graphed on a number line with an OPEN dot?

hints: For each amount, find the point on the graph where f(b) equals it, and read its b-value.
“At least” includes the boundary; “less than” does not.
An open dot means the boundary is not a solution.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. “At least $925” means total sales of…

steps.title: Open or closed
steps.instruction: A closed dot means the boundary value is a solution (≤ or ≥). An open dot means it is not (< or >).

reasoning: Only the strict inequality, b < 540, uses an open dot.
solutionReview.commonError: Reversing the symbol when nothing negative was multiplied or divided — 3.75 is positive.

questions.prompt: Honors — Two fundraisers. The troop could sell scented candles instead: each candle earns $5, with no starting credit, so candle sales are c(b) = 5b. The graph shows c(b) and Elijah’s popcorn sales f(b) = 3.75b + 25 for b items sold. Use the graph and the equations.

responses.label: The point where the two graphs meet
An inequality for the numbers of items b for which candles earn MORE than popcorn
The least whole number of items for which candles earn more
Explain the graph: for those numbers of items…
options: the candle graph is above the popcorn graph, because candles earn more for each item sold
the popcorn graph is above the candle graph
the popcorn credit makes popcorn earn more forever
responses.answer: the candle graph is above the popcorn graph, because candles earn more for each item sold

hints: Find where the two graphs cross, then read both coordinates.
“Candles earn more” means 5b is greater than 3.75b + 25. Solve that inequality.
Only whole numbers of items can be sold: test the boundary and the next whole number.

steps.title: Comparing two functions
steps.instruction: f(x) > g(x) is true exactly for the inputs where the graph of f is ABOVE the graph of g. The graphs meet where f(x) = g(x); solving the inequality algebraically finds the same inputs exactly.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. On a graph, “candles earn more than popcorn” means the candle graph is…

attemptFeedback: Set up 5b > 3.75b + 25 and collect the b-terms on one side.
At the crossing point the two sales are equal — that number of items is NOT a solution of “more than”.

reasoning: The graphs meet where 5b = 3.75b + 25: 1.25b = 25, so b = 20 and both sales are $100 — the point (20, 100).
Candles earn more when 5b > 3.75b + 25, so 1.25b > 25 and b > 20.
The least whole number of items is 21: candles $105, popcorn $103.75.
To the right of the crossing the candle graph is above, because its rate ($5 per item) is greater than popcorn’s ($3.75).
solutionReview.commonError: Answering 20 — at 20 items the sales are equal, not more.

questions.prompt: Activity 3.2 — To make the first deposit on the trip, Elijah’s total sales, f(b), need to be at least $1,100. Solve 3.75b + 25 ≥ 1100 for b. Keep the boundary exact (a fraction is fine).
hints: Undo the starting credit first, on both sides.
Then divide both sides by the price per box. Is it positive or negative?

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The first step to isolate b in 3.75b + 25 ≥ 1100 is to…

steps.title: Solving an inequality
steps.instruction: To solve an inequality means to determine the values of the variable that make it true. Isolate the variable on one side of the inequality symbol, just as you would for an equation.

reasoning: Subtract 25 from both sides: 3.75b ≥ 1075.
Divide both sides by 3.75 (positive, so the symbol stays): b ≥ 860/3, about 286.67.
solutionReview.commonError: Rounding the boundary in the middle of solving — keep it exact until you interpret it.

questions.prompt: Your solution is b ≥ 860/3, about 286.67. How many boxes does Elijah need to sell to make the first deposit?

responses.label: The least number of boxes Elijah can sell to make the deposit
Total sales, in dollars, for that many boxes
Total sales, in dollars, for one box fewer
Why is the answer not 286?
options: 286 is not a solution because it is even.
The inequality uses ≥, so you subtract 1.

hints: Elijah can only sell whole boxes. Which whole numbers are in the solution set?
Substitute your number of boxes into f(b) = 3.75b + 25 and compare with the goal.
Then try one box fewer.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The solution set is every number of boxes from a little above 286 up. Is 286 boxes in it?

reasoning: b ≥ 286.67 and b is a whole number, so the least number of boxes is 287.
solutionReview.commonError: Rounding 286.67 to the nearest whole number gives 287 here by luck; the rule is to choose the least whole number that makes the inequality true.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. “Still not $600 in sales” means total sales that are…

questions.prompt: Activity 3.3 — Elijah’s troop hikes down from their campsite to the base of the mountain. Model the troop’s elevation h(m) after m minutes, complete the table, graph the model, and state the reasonable domain and range.
questions.scenario: The campsite is at an elevation of 4,800 feet and the base of the mountain is at sea level, 0 feet. The troop hikes down at a rate of 20 feet per minute.
questions.equationPrompt: Write the function h(m) for the troop’s elevation after m minutes.
questions.domainPrompt: Write the reasonable domain as an inequality in m.
questions.rangePrompt: Write the reasonable range as an inequality in h.
hints: The elevation goes DOWN as time goes up, so the rate of change is negative.
The hike ends when the troop reaches sea level.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. As the minutes go by, the troop’s elevation…

reasoning: The elevation starts at 4,800 feet and drops 20 feet each minute: h(m) = 4800 − 20m.
Solve 4800 − 20m = 0: the hike ends after 240 minutes.
Domain 0 ≤ m ≤ 240 and range 0 ≤ h ≤ 4800.
solutionReview.commonError: Writing +20m — losing elevation makes the rate of change negative.

questions.prompt: The troop’s elevation after m minutes is h(m) = 4800 − 20m feet. Find the slope, the y-intercept and the x-intercept, and choose what each one means in this situation.

responses.label: Slope
What the slope means
options: The troop descends 20 feet each minute.
The troop climbs 20 feet each minute.
The troop starts 20 feet above sea level.
responses.answer: The troop descends 20 feet each minute.

responses.label: y-intercept (the value of h when m = 0)
What the y-intercept means
options: The campsite is at an elevation of 4,800 feet.
The troop descends 4,800 feet each minute.
responses.answer: The campsite is at an elevation of 4,800 feet.

responses.label: x-intercept (the value of m when h = 0)
What the x-intercept means
options: The troop reaches sea level after 240 minutes.
The troop starts 240 feet above sea level.
The troop descends 240 feet each minute.
The troop has hiked 240 feet when it starts.
responses.answer: The troop reaches sea level after 240 minutes.

hints: In h(m) = (start) + (rate)·m, the coefficient of m is the slope.
To find the x-intercept, set h(m) equal to zero and solve for m.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The y-intercept of h(m) is the elevation when…

reasoning: The coefficient of m, −20, is the rate: the troop descends 20 feet per minute.
h(0) = 4800: the campsite is at 4,800 feet.
4800 − 20m = 0 gives m = 240: the troop reaches sea level after 240 minutes.
solutionReview.commonError: Giving the slope as 20 — the elevation decreases, so the slope is negative.

questions.prompt: When is the troop below 3,200 feet? Solve 4800 − 20m < 3200 for m. Then graph its solution.
hints: Undo the starting elevation first, on both sides.
You will divide both sides by a negative number. What must happen to the symbol?
Check with a time from your solution: is the troop below 3,200 feet then?

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. After subtracting 4800 from both sides, you divide both sides by −20. The symbol…

reasoning: Subtract 4800 from both sides: −20m < −1600.
Divide both sides by −20 and reverse the symbol: m > 80.
In context the hike lasts 240 minutes, so the troop is below 3,200 feet for 80 < m ≤ 240.
solutionReview.commonError: Writing m < 80: dividing by −20 reverses the symbol.

questions.prompt: Each statement about the troop’s elevation h(m) = 4800 − 20m matches an inequality about the minutes m. Solve each one for m (ignore the end of the hike), then compare the symbols.

responses.label: h(m) > 3200 means…
h(m) ≥ 1600 means…
h(m) < 800 means…
h(m) ≤ 4000 means…
What do you notice about the symbols in each row?
Why does that happen?
options: Solving for m divides both sides by −20, a negative number.
responses.answer: Solving for m divides both sides by −20, a negative number.

hints: Replace h(m) with 4800 − 20m and solve, as you did for 3,200 feet.
Every row divides by the same negative number.
Higher elevations happen EARLIER in the hike.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The troop is higher up the mountain…

reasoning: Every row reverses the symbol, because solving divides both sides by −20.
In context: a higher elevation (h greater) means fewer minutes (m less).
solutionReview.commonError: Keeping the symbol pointing the same way after dividing by −20.

questions.prompt: Honors — Between two elevations. The troop’s elevation is h(m) = 4800 − 20m feet after m minutes. Their radios work only while they are BELOW 3,200 feet and ABOVE 2,000 feet. Solve both inequalities on paper, then graph every time m when the radios work and write it as one compound inequality, with the smaller number first.
hints: Write one inequality for each condition: 4800 − 20m < 3200 and 4800 − 20m > 2000.
Each solve divides both sides by −20, so each symbol reverses.
The times that satisfy BOTH conditions lie between the two boundaries — and the boundaries themselves are not included.

steps.title: Compound inequality
steps.instruction: When a quantity must satisfy two conditions at once, its solution set is where both solution sets overlap. Write it as one statement, such as a < m < b, with the smaller number on the left.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. “Below 3,200 feet” for the elevation 4800 − 20m is the inequality…

attemptFeedback: Solve each inequality separately first; each one reverses when you divide by −20.
Keep only the times that satisfy both inequalities, with open dots at both boundaries.

reasoning: Both: 80 < m < 140 — open dots at 80 and 140, shaded between.
solutionReview.commonError: Keeping both symbols after dividing by −20, which gives the impossible “m < 80 and m > 140”.

questions.prompt:
Activity 3.4 — Victoria and Kai each solved 5x + 2 ≥ 3x − 10.
Victoria:  2x + 2 ≥ −10  →  2x ≥ −12  →  x ≥ −6
Kai:  2 ≥ −2x − 10  →  12 ≥ −2x  →  −6 ≤ x

responses.label: Victoria’s first step…
Kai’s first step…
Kai’s last step divides both sides by…
Victoria wrote x ≥ −6 and Kai wrote −6 ≤ x. These…
options: are different because the symbols point different ways
are different because Kai divided by a negative

responses.label: Check x = 0: the value of 5x + 2
Check x = 0: the value of 3x − 10

hints: Compare each student’s first line with the original inequality: which x-term disappeared?
Kai’s last line came from dividing by the coefficient of x in 12 ≥ −2x.
Read −6 ≤ x from the variable’s point of view: x is greater than or equal to −6.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. −6 ≤ x says the same thing as…

steps.title: Variables on both sides
steps.instruction: Solve an inequality with variables on both sides the way you solve an equation: collect the variable terms on one side. Reverse the symbol only if you multiply or divide by a negative number.

reasoning: Victoria subtracted 3x from both sides, so her x-coefficient stayed positive and she never reversed the symbol.
Kai subtracted 5x, leaving −2x; dividing by −2 reversed ≥ into ≤: −6 ≤ x.
x ≥ −6 and −6 ≤ x are the same solution set. At x = 0: 2 ≥ −10 is true.
solutionReview.commonError: Thinking Kai is wrong because his symbol points the other way — read it from the variable’s side.

questions.prompt:
Aaliyah and Ava each solved −4(x − 6) < 22.
Aaliyah:  −4x + 24 < 22  →  −4x < −2  →  x > 1/2
Ava:  x − 6 > −5.5  →  x > 0.5

responses.label: Which step of Aaliyah’s reverses the symbol?
Ava’s first step…
options: divides both sides by −4 and reverses the symbol
responses.answer: divides both sides by −4 and reverses the symbol

responses.label: The boundary value of the solution, as a decimal
Solving an inequality with the distributive property compares to solving an equation like this:
options: The steps are the same, but the symbol reverses whenever you multiply or divide by a negative.
You may never distribute in an inequality.
You must always divide before you distribute.
The symbol reverses whenever you distribute.
responses.answer: The steps are the same, but the symbol reverses whenever you multiply or divide by a negative.

hints: Look for the step in each solution where a negative number divides both sides.
Ava divided −4(x − 6) by −4 first. What happened to the symbol?
To write the boundary as a decimal, divide its numerator by its denominator.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Distributing −4 to (x − 6) changes the inequality symbol?

reasoning: Aaliyah: distributing does not change the symbol; dividing by −4 does: −4x < −2 → x > 1/2.
Ava: dividing both sides by −4 first reverses < into >: x − 6 > −5.5, so x > 0.5.
Both reach the same solution: x > 1/2.
solutionReview.commonError: Reversing the symbol while distributing — only multiplying or dividing BOTH sides by a negative reverses it.

questions.prompt: Talk the Talk — It’s About Solutions, More or Less. Suppose A < B. Sort each statement: is it always true, sometimes true, or never true?
hints: Test with numbers: take A = 2 and B = 5, then try a positive C and a negative C.
Adding or subtracting the same number keeps the order.
Multiplying by a negative number reverses the order; multiplying by a positive keeps it.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. If 2 < 5, which statement is true?

reasoning: Adding or subtracting C on both sides never changes the order: always true.
Multiplying by C keeps the order when C is positive and reverses it when C is negative: AC < BC and AC > BC are each sometimes true.
Multiplying both sides by −1 reverses the order: −A > −B is always true, so −A < −B is never true.
A < B means A − B is negative, so A − B > 0 is never true.
solutionReview.commonError: Deciding AC < BC is always true without testing a negative C.

questions.prompt: Talk the Talk — Honors. In kx + 3 > 7, the letter k stands for a number that is not known yet. Reason about how k decides the solution set, and justify each answer with what you know about inequalities.

responses.label: If k is positive, the solution set of kx + 3 > 7 is…
If k is negative, the solution set is…
The value of k for which the solution set is x < −2
If k = 0, the inequality becomes 3 > 7, so its solution set is…

hints: Subtract 3 from both sides first: kx > 4.
Dividing by a positive k keeps the symbol; dividing by a negative k reverses it.
For the third part: that solution set has a reversed symbol, so k is negative — then set the boundary 4/k equal to the number in that solution set.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Subtracting 3 from both sides of kx + 3 > 7 gives…

attemptFeedback: After kx > 4, decide the symbol by the SIGN of k before you divide.
For x < −2 the boundary is 4/k, and the symbol reversed.

reasoning: k > 0: divide and keep the symbol: x > 4/k. k < 0: divide and reverse it: x < 4/k.
x < −2 needs k < 0 and 4/k = −2, so k = −2.
k = 0: 0 + 3 > 7 is false for every x — no solution.
solutionReview.commonError: Dividing by k without asking whether k is negative — the sign of k decides the direction of the symbol.
